question: what is history
why do we study history
why is history important
answer: History is the study of what happened in the past. We learn it so we can understand how we got here, honour the people who came before us, and make wiser choices in the future.

question: who built the pyramids
why were the pyramids built
tell me about the pyramids of egypt
what are the pyramids
answer: The ancient Egyptians built the pyramids as grand tombs for their pharaohs (kings). The Great Pyramid of Giza was built about 4,500 years ago and was the tallest building in the world for thousands of years!

question: what are hieroglyphics
what is the rosetta stone
how did the egyptians write
answer: Hieroglyphics were the picture writing of ancient Egypt. The Rosetta Stone, found in 1799, had the same message in three scripts, which helped scholars finally read hieroglyphics.

question: who was tutankhamun
who was king tut
who was cleopatra
answer: Tutankhamun was a young Egyptian pharaoh who became king at about nine years old, and his tomb was found full of treasure in 1922. Cleopatra was the famous last active queen of ancient Egypt.

question: who was mansa musa
who was the richest man in history
tell me about mansa musa
answer: Mansa Musa was the emperor of the Mali Empire in the 1300s, and he's thought to be one of the richest people ever. In 1324 he made a famous pilgrimage to Mecca with so much gold that he changed its value in Egypt!

question: what was the mali empire
what is timbuktu
tell me about timbuktu
what was the songhai empire
answer: The Mali Empire and later the Songhai Empire were great West African empires that grew rich from gold and salt trade. Timbuktu, in Mali, was a famous centre of learning with libraries full of old manuscripts.

question: what is great zimbabwe
what was the kingdom of kush
what was the kingdom of aksum
what was the kingdom of benin
what are the benin bronzes
answer: Africa has many great ancient kingdoms: Kush (in Sudan) built its own pyramids, Aksum (in Ethiopia) was a trading power, Great Zimbabwe was a stone city, and the Kingdom of Benin in Nigeria is famous for its beautiful bronze sculptures, the Benin Bronzes.

question: what was the berlin conference
what is colonialism
what was colonialism in africa
what is scramble for africa
answer: Colonialism is when one country takes control of another land and its people. At the Berlin Conference of 1884 to 1885, European powers drew up borders and carved Africa into colonies without asking Africans. Over the 1900s, African countries fought for and won their independence.

question: what was the year of africa
when did african countries get independence
what happened in 1960 in africa
answer: 1960 is called the Year of Africa, because 17 African countries became independent that year, including Nigeria, Senegal and Côte d'Ivoire. Ghana had led the way in 1957.

question: what is the african union

what was the oau
what is pan-africanism
answer: The African Union (AU) is an organisation of African countries that work together for peace and growth. It replaced the Organisation of African Unity (OAU), formed in 1963, where Kwame Nkrumah was a key voice for African unity, called Pan-Africanism.

question: who is nelson mandela
who was nelson mandela
tell me about nelson mandela
answer: Nelson Mandela (1918 to 2013) fought against apartheid in South Africa and spent 27 years in prison. After he was freed in 1990, he became South Africa's first black president in 1994 and won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1993.

question: what was apartheid
what is apartheid
answer: Apartheid was a cruel system in South Africa, from 1948 to the early 1990s, which separated people by race and treated black people unfairly. Brave people, like Nelson Mandela, worked to end it.

question: who was martin luther king
tell me about martin luther king
what was the i have a dream speech
answer: Martin Luther King Jr. was an American leader who worked peacefully for equal rights for black people. In 1963 he gave the famous 'I Have a Dream' speech about a world where all children are treated fairly.

question: who was mahatma gandhi
tell me about gandhi
what is peaceful protest
answer: Mahatma Gandhi led India's peaceful struggle for independence from Britain, which India won in 1947. He believed in non-violence and showed that peaceful protest can change the world.

question: when was world war one
what was world war one
what was world war 1
answer: World War One was a huge war fought mostly in Europe from 1914 to 1918, and many countries took part, including soldiers from the Gold Coast and other African colonies.

question: when was world war two
what was world war two
what was world war 2
when did world war two end
answer: World War Two was fought from 1939 to 1945. It involved most countries of the world, and many soldiers from Africa, including Ghana's Gold Coast Regiment, fought too. Afterwards, the United Nations was set up to help keep peace.

question: what is the united nations
when was the united nations founded
what does the un do
answer: The United Nations (UN) is an organisation of almost every country in the world, set up in 1945 after World War Two to keep peace, protect human rights and help people. Kofi Annan of Ghana led it for ten years.

question: who discovered america
what did columbus do
who was christopher columbus
when did columbus reach america
answer: Christopher Columbus, an Italian explorer sailing for Spain, reached the Caribbean in 1492. But people had lived in the Americas for thousands of years already, so he did not truly 'discover' it.

question: what was the industrial revolution
when was the industrial revolution
what is the industrial revolution
answer: The Industrial Revolution began in Britain around 1760. Steam engines and machines in factories changed how people made things, travelled and lived.

question: who invented the printing press
when was the printing press invented
answer: Johannes Gutenberg in Germany invented the movable-type printing press around 1440. It let books be made quickly and shared ideas far and wide.

question: who was the first person on the moon

when did we land on the moon
who was neil armstrong
answer: Neil Armstrong was the first person to walk on the Moon, on 20th July 1969, during the Apollo 11 mission. He said, 'That's one small step for man, one giant leap for mankind.'

question: who was the first person in space
who was yuri gagarin
who was the first woman in space
who was valentina tereshkova
answer: Yuri Gagarin of the Soviet Union was the first human in space, in 1961. Valentina Tereshkova was the first woman in space, in 1963.

question: who were the ancient romans

what is the colosseum
who was julius caesar
answer: The Romans built a huge empire around the Mediterranean Sea over 2,000 years ago. They made roads, aqueducts and the Colosseum, an arena in Rome for games. Julius Caesar was a famous Roman general and leader.

question: who were the ancient greeks

what is democracy in ancient greece
when did the olympics start
answer: Ancient Greece gave us democracy (in Athens), theatre, philosophy and the Olympic Games, which began in Olympia in 776 BC. The modern Olympics started in 1896.

question: what is the great wall of china
how long is the great wall of china
why was the great wall built
answer: The Great Wall of China is a very long wall of stone and brick built over many centuries to protect ancient China from invaders. All its sections together stretch for thousands of kilometres.

question: what is writing

when was writing invented
what is cuneiform
answer: Writing was invented around 5,000 years ago. The Sumerians of ancient Mesopotamia pressed wedge-shaped marks into clay tablets, called cuneiform, and the Egyptians used hieroglyphics.

question: when was slavery abolished

when did britain abolish the slave trade
answer: Britain made the slave trade illegal in 1807 and abolished slavery in its empire in 1833. Africans and others who had been enslaved, and people who campaigned, like Olaudah Equiano, played a huge part in ending it.

question: when did the berlin wall fall
what was the berlin wall
what was the cold war
answer: The Berlin Wall divided the city of Berlin in Germany from 1961. It came down in 1989, which led to Germany being reunited in 1990, near the end of the Cold War.

question: who was queen nzinga
who was shaka zulu
who were great african leaders
who were famous african queens
answer: Africa has had many great leaders: Queen Nzinga of Angola resisted Portuguese rule, Shaka was the great Zulu king, Yaa Asantewaa of Ghana defended the Golden Stool, and Queen Amina of Zazzau (Zaria) was a famed warrior queen.
